answer: In an agent market for sparrow sightings, the governance inlet requires each identity to lock tokens, and votes are weighted by locked value. A swarm of aliases backed by a whisper of capital still gets only that capital’s voting weight: splitting 100 tokens across 100 agents gives no more power than one agent holding 100. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize a large share of the staked tokens, paying purchase and opportunity costs.
